hints: A palindrome reads the same backwards as forwards. A key observation is that a palindrome mirrors around its center.
There are 2n - 1 possible centers for a string of length n (n single characters for odd-length palindromes, and n - 1 spaces between characters for even-length palindromes).
Expand around each center as long as the mirrored characters match, updating the maximum palindrome found so far.
Can you optimize further using dynamic programming or Manacher's algorithm for linear time?
title: Maximum-Length Palindromic Segment

notes: The judge accepts any substring that is a palindrome and has maximal length for the input.
Do not perform case folding or remove non-alphanumeric characters; use the string as-is.
If your solution returns any longest palindrome, it will be considered correct.
constraints: s consists of ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z) and digits (0-9) only
Return any one longest palindromic substring when multiple valid answers exist
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]. Example: ["babad"]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised return value (string). Example: "bab"

sampleTestCases.explanation: The substring "bab" reads the same in both directions and has length 3. "aba" is another valid longest answer.
The longest palindromic contiguous segment is "bb". No longer substring of "cbbd" is a palindrome.

content.problemStatement:
You receive a string s, output a longest contiguous substring that reads identically from left to right and right to left. If several substrings have the largest length, returning any one of them is valid.

Character comparison is case-sensitive. A substring must occupy consecutive positions in s. Aim for O(n^2) time or better.

notes: All hidden test cases are concrete and use the documented JSON argument format.

solution.approach: Expand around center: A palindrome mirrors around its center. For a string of length n, there are 2n - 1 potential centers (n single-character centers for odd-length palindromes and n - 1 between-character centers for even-length palindromes). We expand outward from each center while characters match, keeping track of the longest palindrome discovered.

optimal.complexity: Time: O(n) using Manacher's algorithm or O(n^2) using expand around center; Space: O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Expand around center checks each of the 2n - 1 possible centers and expands outward in O(n) per center, resulting in O(n^2) time and O(1) extra space. Manacher's algorithm can further optimize this to linear O(n) time by reusing previously computed palindrome radii.

better.description: Dynamic Programming: Let dp[i][j] be true if substring s[i..j] is a palindrome. dp[i][j] = true if s[i] == s[j] and (j - i < 2 or dp[i+1][j-1]). While correct and structured, it requires O(n^2) table space.

bruteForce.description: Examine all O(n^2) substrings and check each one for the palindrome property in O(n) time, yielding O(n^3) overall complexity.

followUps: Can you solve this in O(n) time using Manacher's Algorithm?
How would you handle finding all distinct palindromic substrings instead of just the longest one?
How would the solution change if the string could be infinitely long or provided as a stream?
